question: If cos x/(1 - sin x)+cos x/(1+ sin x) = 4, 0° < x < 90°, then find the value of (tan x + cosec x).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The expression **cos x / (1 − sin x) + cos x / (1 + sin x)** simplifies to **2 / cos x**.

Given: 2 / cos x = 4 ⇒ cos x = 2 / 4 = 1/2.

In the range 0° [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cos x / (1 − sin x) + cos x / (1 + sin x) = 4 and 0° [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b5f4169a03a6d5a9b59761208d8fb5530238a49ab3dd065589f802456c69b9bc.png] 

⇒ cos x [ (1 + sin x + 1 − sin x) / ( (1 − sin x)(1 + sin x) ) ] = 4

⇒ cos x [ 2 / (1 − sin²x) ] = 4

⇒ cos x [ 2 / cos²x ] = 4

⇒ 2 / cos x = 4

⇒ cos x = 2 / 4 = 1/2

⇒ **x = 60°** (Since 0° [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin²x + cos²x = 1, 1 + tan²x = sec²x, and 1 + cot²x = cosec²x.

Standard Values at 60°

sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 60° = √3, and cosec 60° = 2/√3.

Rationalization

To rationalize a denominator like √a, multiply both numerator and denominator by √a.</p
